clue.text: Liking opening of public transport

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only the start of public is used

parts.note: to transport someone is to delight or enchant them

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a fondness for the start of a bus or train journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking for something is a fondness or inclination towards it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Shocking act of men consumed by hatred

indicators.note: something consumed by another is swallowed up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: hatred is enmity
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: A dreadful deed committed by men eaten up with hate.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity can mean a monstrous or outrageous wicked act, a sense apart from great size.

clue.text: Being concerned about link to a time, use this method?

indicators.note: one word put about others wraps round them, so a piece sits inside

parts.note: being concerned for someone is caring
a link or tie is a bond

explanation.surface: A scientist anxious to tie an object to a date asks whether this technique should be used.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay tells you what the method does: it links a sample to a time, which makes the question mark definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiocarbon measurement is the familiar scientific technique for assigning an age to organic remains.

clue.text: Luxuriant hairstyle adopted by a poet getting cut

indicators.note: something adopted by another is taken in, so it is placed inside
a word that is cut loses its tail, here the final letter

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
a bun is a hairstyle with the hair coiled at the back

explanation.surface: A poet's lush hairstyle gets trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' is the container signal and 'getting cut' takes the last letter off the poet; 'Luxuriant' looks like it describes the hair but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxuriant growth is plentiful and rich, so abundant is a close synonym.

clue.text: Holding spades like this, thrust into mound

indicators.note: one piece holding others has them inside it

parts.note: to thrust something into a place is to tuck it there
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
so can mean in this way, like this

explanation.surface: A gardener jams spades into a pile of earth in a particular way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a tufted clump of grass forming a small raised mound.

clue.text: Wife has secret champion

parts.note: inner thoughts are private, secret ones

explanation.surface: A married woman hides a victory of her own.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the victor of a contest, someone who comes first.

clue.text: Handle success, investing pounds

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the pounds are placed inside

parts.note: a hit is a success, as of a show or song
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A trader manages a profitable deal by putting money in.
explanation.definitionFit: The hilt is the handle of a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Stock-picker's reputation is ruined, getting come-uppance

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: one's name is one's reputation
something that rots is ruined

explanation.surface: A stock market trader's good name is destroyed when he finally gets his just deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: The stock is goods in a store, not shares; 'getting come-uppance' turns NAME ROTS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeman looks after stores and picks stock items from the shelves when they are ordered.

clue.text: Marriage is with Democrat finally, not Republican

parts.note: a marriage is a union

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A politician considers a marriage to a Democrat but not to a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: In Northern Ireland politics a Unionist wants to stay in the UK, the opposite of a Republican who wants a united Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish politics loyalists who favour the British link are the traditional opponents of republicans.

clue.text: Forbidding party before return game

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the game's letters run backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone stern holds a party before a second match.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbidding manner is grim and unwelcoming, which is what a dour person is.

clue.text: Bows to priest, dropping head in acknowledgment of father, naturally

parts.note: bends is to bows, as in bowing low

indicators.note: a word dropping its head loses its first letter

parts.note: a minister is a clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone bows to a clergyman whose head drops in acknowledgement of a father.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry a bend sinister was said to mark illegitimacy; a natural child is one born out of wedlock, so 'naturally' is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal band on a coat of arms popularly taken to show a bearer was born outside marriage.

clue.text: Emergency choice as husband finds nowhere to sit

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute picked when the first choice is unavailable
a groom is a new husband

explanation.surface: A last-minute replacement husband turns up at a wedding to find all seats taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Space where an audience must stand because every seat is taken; the phrase describes the lack of seating.

clue.text: Remarkably naive about northern capital

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the extra piece, which sits inside them
something done remarkably is out of the ordinary, so these letters change their usual order

explanation.surface: A credulous visitor is struck by a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remarkably' rearranges NAIVE to VIENA and 'about' puts N inside after VIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian capital city on the Danube.

clue.text: Brief communication to a parent, something spicy

parts.note: a card carries a short message
mom is the American word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone sends a quick note to their mother, a peppery one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic spice from the seeds of a plant in the ginger family.

clue.text: Succession of relatives extremely dirty and unpleasant

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: unpleasant means nasty

explanation.surface: A feuding family line is described as filthy and disagreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers or powerful people from the same family, passing power down.

clue.text: Tried desperately to stop special troops' failure

indicators.note: a piece that stops a gap is plugged inside it
doing something desperately is frantic and disordered, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: the SAS is Britain's Special Air Service, its elite special forces

explanation.surface: Special forces made frantic attempts to halt a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' is the anagram signal and 'to stop' the container; DITER is the shuffled fodder, plugged by the special forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a total failure, a flop or fiasco.

clue.text: Prisoner going to eat in hearing — such punishment?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: something in hearing is heard spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to eat a meal is to dine

explanation.surface: A convict about to eat in court wonders about his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark says the definition is an example: condign is the word classically paired with punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Condign means fitting and deserved, and the stock phrase is condign punishment.

clue.text: Resident commander is unable to keep up

parts.note: OC is the abbreviation for officer commanding

indicators.note: one piece keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: can't means is unable

explanation.surface: An officer living in the house cannot keep pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of a place is its occupant, the person living there.

clue.text: Water fowl round lake showing disease

indicators.note: geese going round the lake surround it, putting it inside

parts.note: ganders are male geese, water birds

explanation.surface: Geese around a lake appear to be ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Glanders is a contagious bacterial disease of horses that can pass to people.

clue.text: Last to leave Holy Land, old victim of Inquisition

indicators.note: the last letter is the one that leaves the word

parts.note: Galilee is a region of the Holy Land

explanation.surface: Someone leaving the biblical lands last is an old victim of persecution.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inquisition tried the astronomer in 1633 for teaching that the earth goes round the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomer was condemned by the Roman Inquisition and kept under house arrest.

clue.text: What's ready to add to casserole? It's apple purée

definitions.text: What's ready to add to casserole?

indicators.note: a purée is food mashed to a pulp, so these letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook asks what goes in the stew and is told it's mashed apple.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried halved peas come ready to throw into stews and casseroles without soaking.

clue.text: Debate giving dog new lead

indicators.note: a dog given a new lead has its first letter replaced

parts.note: bow-wow is a nursery word for a dog

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over buying the dog a new leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new lead' swaps the first letter, B, for P; the P is not otherwise clued, the substitution simply making a real word.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is a meeting for discussion, originally a North American gathering of councillors.

clue.text: Emphatically know how to dance

indicators.note: saying something emphatically repeats it for force, so the word appears twice

parts.note: can means know how to, as in can swim

explanation.surface: Someone insists that they really do know how to dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking dance of Parisian music halls.

clue.text: Ostensibly quiet words heard all over the house

definitions.text: Ostensibly quiet words heard all over the house

parts.words: Ostensibly quiet words heard all over the house
parts.note: the house is a theatre auditorium, where an actor's supposedly hushed aside must still reach every seat

explanation.walkthrough: The house is the theatre audience, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside delivered on stage as if hushed but loud enough for the whole audience.

clue.text: Primate installs son in area of church

indicators.note: to install something is to put it in place inside

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey settles a boy in a corner of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is a semicircular recess, usually at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Follow medal play to the end

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: going to the end of a word takes just its last letter

explanation.surface: An honoured actor sees a play through to its finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow rules or orders is to obey them.

clue.text: In European tradition, wicked behaviour played out here?

indicators.note: one piece placed in others sits inside them

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge
sin is wicked behaviour

explanation.surface: A story of misdeeds steeped in European folklore is acted out somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet, full of wicked behaviour, is played out at Elsinore, the Danish castle where it is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Hamlet is set in the Danish royal castle at Helsingør, anglicised in the play.

clue.text: Pangloss was plump, as shown by one film

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
I is the Roman numeral for one
a film is a thin layer, such as a mist

explanation.surface: A character's weight is the subject of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Pangloss is the tutor in Voltaire's Candide who holds that all is for the best; 'plump' is a verb, not about weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's Pangloss is the classic figure of relentless hopefulness, insisting all is for the best.
